summary: I raise nothing at any severity, and I record what I attacked rather than resting on an empty finding list. My v5 advisory is repaired in both limbs and past what I proposed: generation, admittedManifestDigest and toolIdentity now exist only inside targetIdentity, which became a discriminated union keyed on action class with per-branch forbiddenMembers, and the toolIdentity destination names the child with an explicit 'Not the targetIdentity object as a whole.' The deadline and byte-cap additions are not invented — doctor v4's own scope member says the bound includes 'which deadline, which byte cap', and v6's per-class requiredness matches v4's per-class prose exactly, byteCap required for CA-1, CA-2 and CA-4-HOST and null-with-reason for CA-3, which is precisely where v4 mentions a deadline only. The union itself mirrors v4's own disjunction, 'component generation + admitted manifest digest, or declared external-system identity'. My sharpest falsification attempt was the reverse direction: v4 says the argument vector is DISCLOSED in the post-report rather than scoped by the consent, and v6 correctly does not scope it — argumentVector occurs zero times. Every regression axis holds.

predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA5-A1: REPAIRED, both limbs, and past what I proposed. Limb one, the dual-home ambiguity: the scope shape now has fifteen members and none of generation, admittedManifestDigest or toolIdentity appears among them — I verified the top-level absence mechanically. targetIdentity is now type 'discriminated-object-or-null' with a union of two branches: when CA-1 its closedMembers are generation and admittedManifestDigest with toolIdentity forbidden, and when CA-2 its closedMembers are toolIdentity with generation and admittedManifestDigest forbidden. It also carries an explicit noTopLevelDuplicates statement: 'generation, admittedManifestDigest, and toolIdentity exist only inside this object. They are not top-level scope members.' I asked for nesting; the union with per-branch forbiddenMembers is stronger, because it makes a CA-2 record carrying a generation a shape violation rather than merely an unused field. The union is also exhaustive over the four classes: CA-1 and CA-2 are branches, and nullWhen covers CA-3 and CA-4-HOST with an explicit reason required. Limb two, the type mismatch: the toolIdentity destination now reads 'consentRecords[].scope.targetIdentity.toolIdentity for CA-2. Not the targetIdentity object as a whole', which is my proposed fix plus the negation of the wrong form.
predecessorFindingVerification.HAE5-CX-01: REPAIRED (repair present; original finding text unseen). The prompt's axis is a closed scope missing doctor-v4's deadline and byte cap. I tested whether the addition is well-founded rather than accepting it. Doctor v4's own scope member semantics reads: 'The exact bound the consent carried: which checks, which target identity (component generation + admitted manifest digest, or declared external-system identity), which enumerated resources, which deadline, which byte cap.' So v5's closed shape, which omitted both while declaring additionalMembers forbidden, would have been incompatible with v4's own scope definition. v6 adds observationDeadline and byteCap, and it preserves v4's authorization distinction verbatim in substance — v4 says these are 'Carried ALONGSIDE the consent but NOT as authorization parameters', and both v6 members carry 'Not an authorization parameter.' byteCap additionally states 'Not the post-report byte counts', correctly distinguishing it from v4's separate top-level bytes member.
predecessorFindingVerification.generation wording (prompt axis, no find: REPAIRED. The string 'will be spawned' occurs zero times in v6. componentGenerationIdentity now reads 'For CA-1 (SPAWN or IN_PROCESS): the exact component generation identity executed or requested. Required on every CA-1 authorization record that produces a consent record, including denied IN_PROCESS attempts.' The v5 phrasing presupposed a spawn, which cannot be true of a denied IN_PROCESS attempt that still produced a consent record; 'executed or requested' covers both without presupposition.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 5934e4437ec751ea17d3300cabb1459fedf96d87aeb970c7b04e22165c3bac00 both times. No drift.
targetIdentity is neither flattened nor duplicated at top level: fifteen scope members, and a mechanical check for generation, admittedManifestDigest and toolIdentity among them returns empty.
CA-2 is not mapped to the whole targetIdentity object: the destination names the child and negates the object form explicitly.

The deadline and byte-cap additions are grounded in doctor v4's scope semantics, not invented, and their per-class requiredness matches v4's per-class prose. v4 describes CA-1 and CA-2 as carrying 'a doctor-side observation deadline and a bound on bytes doctor will accept from the component'; CA-4 as carrying 'a doctor-side observation deadline and a byte bound in both directions'; and CA-3 as carrying 'a doctor-side observation deadline' alone. v6's byteCap is requiredWhen CA-1, CA-2, CA-4-HOST and nullWhen CA-3 with explicit reason. That is an exact match to where v4 does and does not mention a byte bound.

The discriminated union mirrors doctor v4's own disjunction rather than imposing a new one: v4's scope names 'which target identity (component generation + admitted manifest digest, OR declared external-system identity)', which is exactly the CA-1 and CA-2 branches v6 declares.

My strongest falsification attempt, in the reverse direction: doctor v4 states that the descriptor-controlled argument vector 'is DISCLOSED in the post-report rather than scoped by the consent'. If v6 had pulled it into the closed scope shape it would have contradicted v4 on a point v4 makes explicitly. It does not — argumentVector occurs zero times in v6 and is absent from the shape. The contract correctly declines to scope something v4 assigns to disclosure.

verdictNote: ACCEPT, with zero findings, and I state affirmatively that I attacked every axis the prompt names and found nothing rather than merely failing to look. Three of my checks were attempts to break repairs and all three held: the scope shape's coverage I tested by extracting every path any destination writes and comparing it to the declared members; the deadline and byte-cap additions I tested against doctor v4's own scope semantics and its per-class bounds prose, where the requiredness matches exactly including the CA-3 exception; and I ran one deliberate reverse test, checking whether the contract had over-reached by scoping the argument vector that v4 assigns to disclosure, which it had not. Across six versions this artifact has taken one blocker and five advisories from me and repaired every one at bytes, twice recording the measurement that exposed the error so it could not recur, and twice returning a repair stronger than the one proposed. I have recorded an explicit acceptanceScope so this verdict is not read as more than it is: it seals nothing, applies nothing, records nothing, discharges no join blocker, and closes neither DR-105 nor DR-114.
